scheduling_explanation:
This is a simulation-only serial peripheral, not a cryptographic reference. Its RESPONSE_WORD is configured independently of MOSI. The trusted harness compares its receive result against that asymmetric word, checks mock MOSI telemetry against an independent expected word, and reconstructs MOSI with a separate passive wire monitor. Both monitors require exactly 32 selected SCK rising edges per frame; clocks with CS high cannot shift serial state. Readout deliberately transmits 0x96a50fc3 and verifies that input capture too.

Only initialize_interface sets SCK low at time zero; sck_pulse owns every later transition. Controls and MOSI are driven while SCK is low, a 10000 ns half-period provides setup, and the mock samples at the next rising edge. Its MISO assignment uses nonblocking assignment, so the shared driver samples 1 ns after the rising edge, following NBA updates. No same-edge testbench input changes race the peripheral. CS deasserts after SCK falls; the harness waits 1 ns before checking frame telemetry so both independent CS monitors settle. Mock simulation state has multiple procedural writers for framing and synchronous reset; this source is not a synthesis input.

Reset takes effect only on a rising SCK with RST_N low. START asserts BUSY and three additional clocks clear it: this latency is an arbitrary driver-test rule, not evidence about recovered hardware. The baseline includes 6 directed and 8 fixed-LCG frames, 75 named checks, 14 frames, and 457 SCK pulses at seed 4313 by default. The driver has a 20 ms watchdog and bounded completion; host compile/simulation processes also have finite timeouts. Fault scenarios exercise reversed transmit and receive order, short/long/split CS selections, unequal scoreboard words, X/Z comparisons, X/Z MISO, and a too-short completion limit. These are driver checks only; passing them does not validate a recovered cryptographic circuit.
